minutes.headline: Sewer Commission cut Crossroads' grease-trap fine to be paid immediately; school waivers put off to July.
minutes.summary: The commission heard Crossroads Plaza's appeal of its daily grease-trap fine and voted to reduce it, payable immediately. It put the schools' grease-trap waiver requests off until July inspection data is in. It also capped Weston & Sampson's DEP-response work at the existing contract and granted Hilltop Farm a waiver. A long open meeting law dispute took up part of the evening, and it was Troy Daniels' last meeting.

public_comment.topic: Appealed the grease-trap fine on behalf of the owner, arguing the town approved the original undersized trap and the owner spent heavily to replace it.
A member's closing remarks on policy, capital planning and keeping rates from being artificially low.

votes.motion: Reduce Crossroads' fine from the original amount to one thousand dollars, paid immediately, fulfilling the penalty.
Authorize Weston & Sampson to go up to the five thousand dollar budget amount if needed, covering a compliant DEP report and the regulation rewrite.
Approve the minutes of the prior Sewer Commission meeting.
Grant Hilltop Farm's request for a waiver from the grease trap regulations without removing the trap.
Have the business manager, after speaking with counsel, send a certified letter about the Wayland kitchen fine per counsel's recommendation.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to reduce Crossroads Plaza's daily grease-trap fine to a lower amount, payable immediately, which fulfils the penalty.
The commission put the schools' grease-trap waiver requests on the second July meeting agenda, after fresh inspection data.
It voted to let Weston & Sampson work up to the existing budget cap on a compliant DEP report and the regulation rewrite.
It granted Hilltop Farm a waiver from the grease-trap regulations without removing the trap, and set a certified letter on the Wayland kitchen fine.
A pump station data scope proposal was tabled, and the open meeting law complaint ended with no resolution.

why_it_matters: Grease-trap fines and waivers decide what local businesses and schools must pay and install, and they bear on sewer system upkeep that ratepayers fund through their sewer bills.
The DEP report work and the pump station data proposal bear on state compliance and on capital planning, which feed into future sewer rates.
watch_next: The second July meeting agenda, when the schools' waiver requests are due to return with fresh inspection data.
A future agenda with a public hearing on the irrigation meter policy and the grease-trap notification wording.
